title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding
reason: Filters low-value branches of an already supplied candidate tree before target verification. A threshold is calibrated from separate target greedy trajectories, with retrieval-tree and EAGLE-3 tree suppliers evaluated independently. Serving/inference only. Evaluation uses greedy decoding, a non-overlapping calibration/evaluation split, main batch size one and extra batch-size-four/eight tests. Output identity is a greedy guarantee; it is not a general stochastic RL guarantee. Transfer to recurrent rollout trees requires current-policy verification and recalibration under policy/reward-workload change. Calibration and verification savings must be amortized rather than reported as demonstrated RL speedup.
evidence_pointer: Section 3 (valuation/filtering and greedy fallback), Section 4 (recurring-workload/calibration protocol) and Section 5 (retrieval and EAGLE-3 results).
review_basis: primary full text: method, verification assumptions and experimental setting

title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
reason: Combines prefill-selected and recent KV entries for draft-side compression, refreshes their selection as generation progresses, and uses an adaptive refresh controller to limit rescoring. Optional sparse-mask training makes the drafter more compressible. Serving/inference of external and KV-based self-drafters on long-input/long-output SPEED-Bench settings, including greedy and stochastic acceptance measurements. Compression is on the draft cache; an unchanged target and correct rejection sampling preserve the target distribution. Decode staleness here means stale within-sequence KV selection, not actor-policy version drift. RL transfer requires policy-aware cache invalidation, refresh-cost accounting and maintenance of any trained drafter.
evidence_pointer: Sections 2–4 (scope, decode staleness, static/dynamic/adaptive refresh), Section 5 and Appendices D–J (settings, latency/quality and compressibility training).
review_basis: primary full text: method, verification assumptions and experimental setting

title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting
reason: Reuses verifier hidden states beyond the first rejection as shifted anchors for parallel blocks from a pretrained diffusion drafter. Positive overlaps attach those blocks to a baseline proposal and merge shared prefixes for a new target verification. Serving/inference with pretrained DFlash drafters and four autoregressive targets, evaluated at temperature zero across eight benchmarks. Rejected-suffix states are speculative proposal hints, not committed KV state or accepted output. Transfer requires correct-prefix target re-verification and bounded extra state/verification width. Nonzero-temperature RL sampling and end-to-end RL gains have not been demonstrated.
evidence_pointer: Sections 3.1–3.3 (shifted anchors and trie construction), 4.1–4.3 (setup and ablations), and the appendix on earliest positive-overlap selection.

title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
reason: Makes tree proposals conditional on each candidate path through a Domino recurrent correction and constructs a high-value tree with a best-first or GPU frontier builder. Verification must maintain tree-correct recurrent as well as attention state. Both single-stream research-harness and SGLang inference experiments are reported. In the served concurrency sweep, a low-concurrency advantage can reverse at larger batches despite longer acceptance. Transfer therefore requires engine-level profiling and tree-correct recurrent-state handling, rather than translating research-harness speedup to RL. The paper does not evaluate target-policy evolution or RL training.
evidence_pointer: Sections 3.2–3.4; 4.4 (numerical agreement); 4.5.1–4.5.4 (serving, concurrency and hybrid recurrent verification); Section 6 (implementation scope and load-budget limitations).

title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
reason: Combines within-block Jacobi refinement with inter-block foresight. An adapter predicts future verifier states and likely acceptance outcomes so that a drafter on another GPU can prepare candidates while the target verifies the preceding block. Serving/inference evidence only. Acceptance is evaluated at temperatures 0 and 1, while the main throughput comparison uses single-request greedy decoding. The pipelined configuration uses a separate drafter GPU, so its latency ratio is not an equal-GPU-cost RL throughput gain. Transfer requires affordable spare placement, current-policy feature compatibility, and an unchanged target acceptance/correction rule; policy refresh and closed-batch RL training were not evaluated.
evidence_pointer: Sections 4.1–4.3 and 5.1–5.6; Appendix E (hardware/serving protocol and correctness checks) and F.3 (lossless verification).

title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
reason: Reads committed hybrid-linear-attention recurrent states using learned position-conditioned queries and low-rank projections, then injects the retrieved context into a DSpark-style drafter through residual fusion. Fixed-target inference on Qwen3.8-27B, one B200 GPU, greedy decoding and concurrency one. The reader is trained against the target recurrent state and does not demonstrate policy-refresh robustness. Transfer to recurrent/hybrid rollout targets requires consistent committed states, rollback handling, and reader maintenance after policy updates. Greedy agreement here is not experimental evidence of stochastic RL sampling equivalence.
evidence_pointer: Sections 3.1–3.2 and 4.1–4.4; Appendix D.2 and the greedy serving/diagnostic protocol.

title: DLoop: Looped Speculative Decoding
